thread:
lucas: :rotating_light: noticing a sudden spike of 5xx (503) from hosted inference; roughly 12-15% p95 errors for the last 6m. multiple runner pods restarted.
ops-bot: ALERT: hosted-api-prod | 5xx rate 14% | /v1/generate | view: https://dash.redwood/alerts/1790
eline: oncall here, looking. which model/pool? any recent deploys or config changes? @sanjay FYI
lucas: model pinned: opens-7b-quant-v2 on pool hosted-eu-west1-ga. last change was a dynbatch tweak rolled ~2h ago (lower latency target). affected pods: infer-runner-eu-gg-1203, infer-runner-eu-gg-1211, infer-runner-eu-gg-1240.
eline: can you paste the last lines of the runner logs for one of the pods? also paste k8s restart reason if available.
lucas: here's the tail from infer-runner-eu-gg-1203:
```
2026-09-12T14:08:33Z infer-runner[1]: kv_prefetch: starting prefetch for ctx=acme/123
2026-09-12T14:08:34Z infer-runner[1]: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: failed to allocate 2.1GiB
2026-09-12T14:08:34Z infer-runner[1]: ERROR: caught segfault in attention_kernel.cu:ip#0
2026-09-12T14:08:34Z kernel: [UFW] task infer-runner:12345 killed by SIGSEGV
2026-09-12T14:08:35Z kubelet: Pod infer-runner-eu-gg-1203 - ContainerExit - reason: OOMKilled
```
eline: thanks. that looks like an OOM followed by segfault during kv prefetch. any recent driver updates on those nodes? @devops
devops: we did a rolling driver update to nvidia-driver 535.12 yesterday evening on eu-west pools, but only ~30% nodes completed. I'm checking node-driver versions now.
sanjay: that trace lines up with a regression in the attention kernel when memory is fragmented after prefetch. also NVML logs show driver resets in the same window. can you collect /var/log/nvidia-installer.log and `dmesg | tail` from one affected node?
oncall: quick mitigation: disable kv prefetch for that model pool and restart runners, and temporarily reduce concurrency/batch size. we have a runtime flag REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH=false that should toggle it without rolling the binary. lucas can you patch the pool config?
lucas: applying patch to pool hosted-eu-west1-ga: `redwoodctl pools update hosted-eu-west1-ga --env REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH=false --restart-runners`
lucas: also executing a pod restart: `kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/infer-runner-eu-gg` (rolling)
devops: paused autoscaler for the pool to prevent noisy resizes. command run: `kubectl scale --replicas=18 deployment/infer-runner-eu-gg --namespace=prod`
maria: CS note: Acme Labs reported timeouts for critical workflows. I told them we're investigating and routing them to dedicated if needed. collecting affected request ids for credit/billing: need list and time window.
eline: can someone grab heap/profile or coredump from one restarted pod? set `kernel.core_pattern` to capture and upload to s3: `echo '/cores/core.%e.%p.%t' > /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern` , then reproduce on a drained node.
sanjay: workaround if OOM is primary: lower `MAX_BATCH_TOKENS` and `CONCURRENCY_PER_GPU` for that runtime. Example envs:
```
MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=2048
CONCURRENCY_PER_GPU=1
```
lucas: changed pool envs (kv_prefetch=false, reduced MAX_BATCH_TOKENS). monitoring: error rate falling to ~3% in last 5m.
oncall: good. keep watch for driver reset patterns. if driver 535.x correlates we'll schedule rollback for eu-west1. also collect `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY` snapshots.
devops: attached nvml excerpt from node-a1:
```
Time: 2026-09-12T14:08:34Z
NVML: Driver shutdown detected. GPU memory allocated: 14.7GiB, reserved: 15.9GiB
```
maria: opened a support ticket for Acme with mitigation notes and ETA. CC'ing commercial. Will follow up on credits once we have final window and root cause.
lucas: note for postmortem: likely interaction of dynbatch tuning + kv prefetch on driver 535.x -> memory fragmentation -> OOM -> kernel crash. need to add prefetch safety check and better eviction.
sanjay: agree. I'll prepare a fastfix: flag to disable prefetch per-model and a guard to refuse >70% GPU reserved memory before prefetch.
ops-bot: ALERT CLEARED: 5xx rate dropped below threshold. (auto)
eline: closing handoff. follow-up actions: collect core, nvml, kernel logs; revert driver or pause further driver rollouts; add canary to dynbatch change. I'll file the incident doc.
lucas: thanks all. keeping thread open for any residuals. :thumbsup:
